title: Rehearsing at the Appomattox Club and who really hired the Johnsons
summary: Randolph found the Johnson brothers, rehearsed the band, and says Jack Oglesby copied record parts, disputing Budd's claim that Armstrong sent for them.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs

blocks.x: While I was getting the band together, somebody told me, says, there's two boys in Chicago here, say, you ought to get them, Randolph. Say, they are good, says. I said, what's their name? And he says, Bud Johnson and Keg Johnson, two brothers. I said, well, send them on down here. Tell them to come down to the Appomatox. We were rehearsing down there. That was down on South Parkway.
It was a club, and that's where I started rehearsing, with the band.
This was before Louis got to town?
Yeah, that's when Louis came in and I got the band together there and rehearsed the band, at the Appomatox Club. And then, Jack Oglesby came down and, now,

Jack Oglesby, he was our -- he used to do a lot of our -- a lot of things that was taken off -- he would take things off of records. He was good for that. He would take things, similar things, off of the record of that first band, that Louis wanted to play.
And Jack would take them off. For this other band, for the big band. And then, you see, I didn't have to fool with that. I never did care for a job like that. That extraction.
Bud says he wrote some arrangements for that band, too. Do you recall that? Bud Johnson.

Well, I don't know. I don't recall anything of Bud's writing. I heard Bud say, when they were playing a tribute to Louis' death, I heard Bud say that Louis sent for he and his brother, but Louis didn't send for he and his brother. I sent for them. Louis didn't know anything about Bud, and I didn't know anything about Bud until -- the Oldham boys told me about Bud Johnson and them, and I send for Bud, I didn't send for -- I mean, Louis didn't know it. Louis had me to get the band together.
But that's some of that stuff that I was telling you about.
Yeah, well, that's what we're trying
to do, set the record straight.
